svg.title: Scene 57: Waves that add and waves that cancel
svg.desc: Four frames, labelled as a water-wave analogy. 1, two stones dropped in a pond send out rings; solid rings are crests and dashed rings troughs; one marked point is where two crests meet, another where a crest meets a trough. 2, where crest meets crest, heights add: plus one plus plus one makes plus two, plotted as two equal waves and their doubled sum. 3, where crest meets trough, plus one plus minus one makes zero: the two waves cancel and the sum is flat. 4, a note that this is an analogy: water heights add here, while in quantum mechanics it is amplitudes, numbers that are not heights of anything, that add (Scene 59).
svg.text: Waves that add and waves that cancel
Heights add point by point. This is the picture to borrow from, carefully.

g.text: Solid ring: crest. Dashed ring: trough. Illustrative.
An analogy, not the thing itself
Here, heights of water add. In quantum mechanics,
amplitudes add: numbers, not the height of anything.
Blue: classical waves (analogy). Curves computed, not drawn by hand.
